newsitem.title: UK: Russian supplies pressure Med oil product markets.
newsitem.headline: Russian supplies pressure Med oil product markets.

text.p: Mediterranean fuel and gas oil markets were pressured by Russian supplies and gasoline prices were steady on Wednesday, traders said.
Gasoline was steady in an uneventful day. Unleaded premium was assessed around $2.50 above fob Med quotes. Demand out of Italy, Lebanon, Turkey and Greece supported the market.
The main products pipeline connecting Fos-sur-Mer to Lyon is closed next week for a routine inspection. Operator TMR said they did not expect any direct impact in operations.
The pipeline serves BP's Lavera, Shell's Berre refinery and Esso's Fos refineries among other.
The Russian gas oil market was still seen pressured with plentiful supplies coming out of the main Black Sea ports. Prices were pegged at high cif quotes evens basis Genoa.
Russian gas oil exports from Baltic and Black Sea terminals almost doubled last week to 460,952 barrels per day.
The market for EN590 was seen tight however with demand from north European refiners.
Fuel oil was dominated by a severe overhang of Russian cracked and straight-run material that weak bunker and refining demand looked unlikely to soak up quickly.

One vessel with a cargo of M-40 has been afloat off Augusta for several days already, unable to find a buyer. Although several more packets were in danger of becoming distressed prices have not yet suffered badly.

"I would have thought we'd have seen lower numbers but that's not yet happened," said one trader. "This material will eventually go somewhere but I don't know where and there is quite a few more stacking up to come down."
Traders said prices had to be $5 lower for the Singapore arbitrage to open and take supplies out of the region.
